question: Which of the following is a famous wildlife spot, that was established in 1981 in Ladakh, and is famous for high population of snow leopards and a wide variety of birds?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hemis National Park**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hemis National Park in Ladakh is a famous wildlife spot that was established in 1981 and is known for its high population of snow leopards and a wide variety of birds: 
 
• Hemis National Park is located in the eastern part of Ladakh, in the state of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It's about 50 km from Leh, one of the capitals of Ladakh. 
 
• The park covers an area of about 4,400 square kilometres. 
 
• The park is home to a variety of wildlife, including snow leopards, Tibetan wolves, Eurasian brown bears, Bharal (blue sheep), Argali (Great Tibetan Sheep), red fox, Himalayan marmot, mountain weasel, and Himalayan mouse hare. 
 
• The park was established to conserve the fragile Himalayan ecosystem and provide a sanctuary for the region's wildlife. 
 
• Visitors can enjoy camping, trekking, and jeep safaris.
 
• The best time to visit is between May and early October, as jeep safaris and trekking routes are stalled after November due to heavy snowfall. 
 
• The park is named after the famous Hemis Monastery, which is located within its boundaries.
 
• The monastery is a cultural and spiritual hub.

• Pin Valley National Park
 
• Located in Lahaul and Spiti District, this park was established in 1987.
 
• It is home to endangered species like the snow leopard and Siberian ibex. 
 
• Namdapha National Park
 
• Established in 1983, this park is located in Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• It is the third largest national park in India and is a biodiversity hotspot in the Eastern Himalayas. 
 
• Established in 1982, this park is located in the Chamoli Garhwal district of Uttarakhand.
 
• It is situated around the peak of Nanda Devi and lies at an elevation of more than 3,500 m (11,500 ft) above mean sea level.
